subject: Post-call: inference suitability & perf links for HealthGrid
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + recommended next steps (inference suitability)

Elena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed next-step plan so we keep momentum.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary workload: clinical triage assistant (short medical notes -> structured intent + next-action suggestions)
- SLOs: 80–120ms p50 on individual text-generation calls for live triage UI; p99 target ~450ms for 99% of requests
- Expected QPS: baseline ~200 req/s with 10% burst to 500; average sequence length ~150 tokens
- Data controls: PHI-in-transit only, need VPC option for pilot later

High-level recommendation (for pilot)
- Candidate model family: open-chat-turbo-series (causal) and a trimmed encoder-decoder for structured extraction
- Redwood-verified profiles I recommend: rwd-open-7B-q8 (balanced latency/cost) and rwd-open-13B-fp16 (higher-quality fallback)
- Suggested runtime config: batching target 32, prefix KV caching for common prompts, autoscale floor for reserved Dedicated pool once pilot is confirmed

Attached I’ve included the concise Redwood performance profile for the two variants, an abbreviated prompt set we used during evaluation, and a small perf report for a 50k request-sim run. Links below go to the same artifacts in Drive + the Redwood benchmark page.

Action items / proposed mutual action plan
1) HealthGrid: share a 2‑week sample of anonymized prompts for accuracy checks (not PHI). Target by Mar 15.
2) Redwood: run a 2k-sample quality regression on rwd-open-7B-q8 + rwd-open-13B-fp16 and share label-level diff. ETA Mar 12.
3) Joint: schedule an 60-min pilot kickoff to shape SLA/burst config (I propose Mar 20).

Risk notes we flagged on the call
- Quality regression risk: rwd-open-7B-q8 has ~3–5% drop in structured extraction F1 vs the 13B at short-context prompts (details in perf report). We can mitigate with prompt templates and a lightweight reranker.
- Latency under burst: without a dedicated floor, p99 shifts up ~2–3x during sustained burst — we can pin capacity for the pilot.

If this plan looks good, I’ll have Marissa run the regression and share a labeled diff + prompt adjustments by next week.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
Schedule: https://cal.com/karthik-iyer/30

Attachments: redwood_profile_healthgrid_v1.json (profile), prompt_set_sample_healthgrid_v2.txt (sample prompts), perf_report_50kreqs.pdf (summary)

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@healthgrid.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: HealthGrid Procurement <procurement@healthgrid.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + recommended next steps (inference suitability)

Karthik — this is perfect, thank you. Appreciate the clear options. A few quick notes:  

- We can provide a de-identified 2-week sample by Mar 14 (Procurement copied for approvals).
- Question on the 7B q8: can you confirm token-level cost delta vs the 13B fp16 for our expected volume? Need it for our internal ROI calc.
- We are sensitive to p99 — our clinical UX team is strict around tail latency. If you can include a few sample tail traces that show p99 behavior during bursts that will help us sell this internally.

I’ll route this to Procurement; Santiago (procurement) will coordinate the PO conversation. Let’s plan to sync the week of Mar 20 for the pilot kickoff.

Best,
Elena
Elena Torres
VP, Product — HealthGrid

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@healthgrid.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 12:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + recommended next steps (inference suitability)

Elena / team — quick follow with the artifacts Karthik referenced and a few technical clarifications:  

1) Cost delta (token-level) — approximate numbers for expected mix (baseline 200 req/s, avg 150 tokens):
   - rwd-open-7B-q8: ~0.6x per-token cost vs 13B-fp16 (est) — roughly 40% savings at generation time when quantized and running with Redwood batching.
   - rwd-open-13B-fp16: higher per-token compute but ~+3–5% absolute quality on structured extraction in our labeled sampling.

2) Performance snapshot (from the perf_report_50kreqs.pdf attached):
   - rwd-open-7B-q8 @ batch=32, seq=150: p50 85ms, p95 320ms, p99 460ms, sustained TPS ~210 (on a 4-GPU dedicated pool with continuous batching).
   - rwd-open-13B-fp16 @ batch=24, seq=150: p50 160ms, p95 540ms, p99 780ms, sustained TPS ~160.

3) Tail behavior during bursts — we included three sample traces in the Drive folder (links below) showing how prefix caching and request shaping keep p99 bounded. Those traces are from a simulated 10-minute 500rps burst; note that without capacity floor p99 increases to ~1.6s in the same sim.

4) Prompt-set notes — the attached prompt_set_sample_healthgrid_v2.txt contains our recommended templates (system + few-shot examples) that reduce hallucinations and improve extraction F1 by ~2 points in the 7B variant. We recommend this be part of your QA pass.

Links (copied to related_links field):
- Redwood benchmark: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/healthgrid-2028
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_healthgrid-eval
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/2384/HG-2028-0421

If you’d like, Jonas and I can run a 60-minute lab session with your engineers on Mar 16 to walk through the prompt tuning and perf traces. Karthik — should we lock Mar 16 for a tech workshop or aim for the Mar 20 kickoff?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: perf_report_50kreqs.pdf, prompt_set_sample_healthgrid_v2.txt, redwood_profile_healthgrid_v1.json

+1 on Mar 16 tech lab if that works for you, Elena. I’ll prepare a short demo that toggles the 7B q8 vs 13B fp16 under a synthetic burst so you can see p99 improvements when we apply the capacity floor and prefix caching.

Jonas
